1	# Windows E2E Tests — Design
2	
3	## Goal
4	
5	Run the existing `e2e/lifecycle_test.go` suite on Windows in CI so we can reproduce and verify Windows-specific bugs (like the one this branch is named for) without leaving the local machine.
6	
7	The same suite already runs on Linux locally. We want:
8	
9	1. A new on-demand workflow (`workflow_dispatch` + `/test-e2e` PR-comment trigger) so e2e doesn't run on every PR.
10	2. An OS matrix of `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest`.
11	3. The interactive `TestLifecycle_InteractiveSession` test to actually work on Windows (not skip), via ConPTY instead of tmux.
12	
13	## Why this isn't a one-line workflow change
14	
15	The e2e package today has three Linux-only assumptions baked in:
16	
17	1. **`e2e/agents/tmux.go`** — drives Kiro/Pi interactive sessions via the `tmux` CLI. Windows has no tmux.
18	2. **`e2e/agents/kiro.go` and `pi.go`** — set `syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}` and call `syscall.Kill(-pid, ...)` on cancellation. Both are POSIX-only — `Setpgid` doesn't exist on `windows/syscall` and `syscall.Kill` doesn't either, so the package won't even **compile** on `GOOS=windows`.
19	3. **`e2e/setup_test.go`** — preflight checks for `tmux` in `PATH`, and sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`. Neither is correct on Windows.
20	
21	So Windows support is: cross-platform refactor of the agent runner + a real ConPTY session impl + a couple of small test-setup fixes + the new workflow.
22	
23	## ConPTY in one paragraph
24	
25	**ConPTY** (Pseudo Console) is the native Windows pseudo-terminal API, available since Windows 10 1809. It's the OS-level thing that makes interactive TUIs work — the equivalent role tmux plays for us on Linux. PowerShell is *not* a substitute: it's a shell that runs *inside* a terminal, not a terminal provider, so child processes started under PowerShell with `Start-Process -RedirectStandardInput` see a pipe (not a TTY) and switch off interactive mode. We need a real PTY, and on Windows that means ConPTY. We'll use [`github.com/UserExistsError/conpty`](https://github.com/UserExistsError/conpty) (MIT, ~470⭐, actively used) as the Go wrapper.
26	
27	ConPTY is lower-level than tmux: it gives us a process attached to a pseudo-console with raw read/write pipes. There's no built-in scrollback buffer and no named keys — we provide both ourselves.
28	
29	## Component plan
30	
31	### 1. Cross-platform process attributes
32	
33	New build-tagged helpers in `e2e/agents/`:
34	
35	- `proc_unix.go` (`//go:build !windows`):
36	  ```go
37	  func configureCmdProcAttr(cmd *exec.Cmd) {
38	      cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}
39	      cmd.Cancel = func() error { return syscall.Kill(-cmd.Process.Pid, syscall.SIGKILL) }
40	  }
41	  ```
42	- `proc_windows.go` (`//go:build windows`):
43	  ```go
44	  func configureCmdProcAttr(cmd *exec.Cmd) {
45	      cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{CreationFlags: 0x00000200} // CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP
46	      cmd.Cancel = func() error { return cmd.Process.Kill() }
47	  }
48	  ```
49	
50	`kiro.go` and `pi.go` `RunPrompt` switch from inline syscall code to `configureCmdProcAttr(cmd)`.
51	
52	Trade-off on Windows: we lose the `kill -pid` semantics that nuke the whole process group. `cmd.Process.Kill()` only kills the leader. For long-lived background TUIs this can leak children; for our short non-interactive `RunPrompt` invocations under context timeout, the child process is the agent itself and that's what we kill.
53	
54	### 2. tmux.go gets `//go:build !windows`
55	
56	Pure compile-out — tmux driver only exists on unix. Single-line change at the top of the file.
57	
58	### 3. ConPTY session
59	
60	New file `e2e/agents/conpty_windows.go` (`//go:build windows`).
61	
62	```go
63	type ConPTYSession struct {
64	    cpty     *conpty.ConPty
65	    procDone <-chan struct{}
66	    exitErr  error
67	
68	    bufMu sync.Mutex
69	    buf   []byte // ANSI-stripped rolling buffer, capped at 64 KiB
70	
71	    cleanups     []func()
72	    stableAtSend string
73	}
74	
75	func NewConPTYSession(name, dir string, unsetEnv []string, command string, args ...string) (*ConPTYSession, error)
76	```
77	
78	Method-by-method:
79	
80	- **`NewConPTYSession`**: builds command-line string (`command arg1 "arg with space" ...`), filters env removing `unsetEnv` entries, calls `conpty.Start(cmdLine, conpty.ConPtyWorkDir(dir), conpty.ConPtyEnv(env))`. Spawns one background goroutine reading from the conpty into the buffer (with mutex), and a second goroutine that calls `cpty.Wait(sessCtx)` and closes a `procDone` channel. (`Wait` takes a `context.Context` — confirmed against `github.com/UserExistsError/conpty v0.1.4` via `go doc`. The session stores its own `context.Background()`-derived `sessCtx` cancelled in `Close()` so `Wait` returns when the session is torn down.)
81	- **`Send(input)`**: mirrors `TmuxSession.Send` exactly — captures pre-state, calls `SendKeys(input)`, sleeps 200ms, calls `SendKeys("Enter")`, then runs the same 5-second "wait for content to change" loop using `stableContent`.
82	- **`SendKeys(keys ...string)`**: per key, look up `translateKey(k)` and write the resulting bytes to the conpty.
83	- **`WaitFor(pattern, timeout)`**: same loop and same `stableContent` settle logic as `TmuxSession.WaitFor`. Detects "process exited" by checking `procDone`.
84	- **`Capture()`**: returns the current ANSI-stripped buffer, trimmed of trailing newlines (matches tmux's `capture-pane -p` shape closely enough for the prompt-pattern regexes the tests use).
85	- **`Close()`**: runs cleanups, closes the conpty (terminates the process).
86	
87	#### Key translator (shared by tmux SendKeys vocabulary)
88	
89	```go
90	func translateKey(k string) string {
91	    switch k {
92	    case "Enter":              return "\r"
93	    case "Tab":                return "\t"
94	    case "Escape", "Esc":      return "\x1b"
95	    case "BSpace", "Backspace": return "\x7f"
96	    case "Up":                 return "\x1b[A"
97	    case "Down":               return "\x1b[B"
98	    case "Right":              return "\x1b[C"
99	    case "Left":               return "\x1b[D"
100	    case "Space":              return " "
101	    }
102	    if len(k) == 3 && (k[0] == 'C' || k[0] == 'c') && k[1] == '-' {
103	        c := k[2]
104	        if c >= 'a' && c <= 'z' { return string([]byte{c - 'a' + 1}) }
105	        if c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z' { return string([]byte{c - 'A' + 1}) }
106	    }
107	    return k // literal text
108	}
109	```
110	
111	Vocabulary chosen to match the tmux key names already used by `TmuxSession.SendKeys`, so test code stays portable.
112	
113	#### ANSI stripping
114	
115	Tests look for prompt patterns like `>` (Kiro) and `\$\d` (Pi) — simple regex matches. We don't need a full terminal emulator. A regex strip of CSI sequences (`\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[a-zA-Z]`) plus OSC sequences (`\x1b\][^\x07]*\x07`) plus stripping `\r` (so CR-rewrites collapse) is sufficient.
116	
117	Caveat: this CSI regex misses sequences with intermediate bytes (e.g. `\x1b[ q` cursor-style, `\x1b[1;2:3:4m` SGR with colon separators) and ST-terminated OSC (`\x1b\\` instead of `BEL`). If a TUI under test emits any of those and the leftover bytes confuse the prompt regexes, the upgrade path is `charmbracelet/x/ansi` which has a tested CSI parser plus a virtual screen. We start simple because the actual prompts (`>` and `\$\d`) are short enough to be unaffected by most stray escape bytes.
118	
119	#### Buffer cap
120	
121	Rolling 64 KiB. When append would overflow, drop the oldest 25 % so we never grow unbounded. Tests don't need long history — only the recent prompt area matters for regex matching.
122	
123	### 4. Session factory
124	
125	Tiny build-tagged constructor so `kiro.go` and `pi.go` don't need build tags themselves:
126	
127	- `e2e/agents/session_unix.go` (`//go:build !windows`):
128	  ```go
129	  func newInteractiveSession(name, dir string, unsetEnv []string, cmd string, args ...string) (Session, error) {
130	      return NewTmuxSession(name, dir, unsetEnv, cmd, args...)
131	  }
132	  ```
133	- `e2e/agents/session_windows.go` (`//go:build windows`):
134	  ```go
135	  func newInteractiveSession(name, dir string, unsetEnv []string, cmd string, args ...string) (Session, error) {
136	      return NewConPTYSession(name, dir, unsetEnv, cmd, args...)
137	  }
138	  ```
139	
140	`Pi.StartSession` / `Kiro.StartSession` switch from `NewTmuxSession(...)` to `newInteractiveSession(...)`. The redundant `s.stableAtSend = ""` lines (it's already the zero value after construction) get dropped — that removes the only direct field access through the concrete tmux type.
141	
142	### 5. setup_test.go cross-platform fixes
143	
144	Two small changes:
145	
146	```go
147	// Old:
148	if _, err := exec.LookPath("tmux"); err != nil { /* warn */ }
149	
150	// New:
151	if runtime.GOOS != "windows" {
152	    if _, err := exec.LookPath("tmux"); err != nil { /* warn */ }
153	}
154	```
155	
156	```go
157	// Old:
158	os.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL", "/dev/null")
159	
160	// New:
161	gc, _ := os.CreateTemp("", "e2e-gitconfig-*")
162	gc.Close()
163	os.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL", gc.Name())
164	// (cleanup on exit via t.Cleanup or defer in TestMain via os.Remove)
165	```
166	
167	Empty temp file is functionally equivalent to `/dev/null` for git's purposes (an empty file = no global config) and works on every OS.
168	
169	### 6. Drop `/tmp` GOCACHE overrides (and the `env` prefix)
170	
171	The existing `mise-tasks/build`, `mise-tasks/test`, and `mise.toml` `test:e2e:lifecycle` task all use `env GOCACHE=/tmp/go-build-cache <command>`. `/tmp` doesn't exist on `windows-latest`, **and** the `env` utility itself is unix-only (cmd.exe / PowerShell don't have it on PATH). Options considered:
172	
173	- **Keep but conditionalize via shell** — messy, three files.
174	- **Use `${TMPDIR}`** — inconsistent across OSes, doesn't fix the `env` issue.
175	- **Drop the entire `env GOCACHE=...` prefix** — Go's default cache (`%LocalAppData%\go-build` on Windows, `~/.cache/go-build` on Linux, `~/Library/Caches/go-build` on macOS) is correct for each OS. Chosen.
176	
177	So `mise.toml`'s `test:e2e:lifecycle` `run = "env GOCACHE=/tmp/go-build-cache go test ..."` becomes `run = "go test ..."`. Removing only the `GOCACHE=...` and leaving `env go test ...` would still break Windows because `env` is not a Windows command — the whole prefix has to go.
178	
179	CI caching can still happen via `actions/cache` keyed on `${{ runner.os }}` if we want it later — orthogonal to this change.
180	
181	Note: `mise-tasks/build` and `mise-tasks/test` are bash scripts (`#!/usr/bin/env bash`). They do **not** run on Windows and the e2e workflow does not invoke them — it runs `mise run test:e2e:lifecycle` directly, which is defined inline in `mise.toml` as a portable `go test ...` command. The reason we still edit the bash scripts is purely to keep `/tmp` references from going stale; if they later get invoked from a Windows context (e.g. cross-compiling), they'd fail anyway for unrelated reasons. Not strictly required for this change — included as defensive cleanup.
182	
183	### 6a. `BuildAgent` on Windows: `.exe` suffix
184	
185	`e2e/build.go` `BuildAgent` produces `binPath := filepath.Join(outputDir, agentName)` and runs `go build -o binPath`. On Windows this would emit a literal extension-less file, which `exec.LookPath` and `cmd.exe`'s `PATHEXT` resolution will not find. Fix:
186	
187	```go
188	binPath := filepath.Join(outputDir, agentName)
189	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
190	    binPath += ".exe"
191	}
192	```
193	
194	Add a corresponding `runtime` import (already imported in this file). This is a near-certainty (not a "verify on first run" item), so it lives in the file-by-file diff rather than the risk table.
195	
196	### 7. Workflow file (`.github/workflows/e2e.yml`)
197	
198	```yaml
199	name: E2E
200	
201	on:
202	  workflow_dispatch:
203	  issue_comment:
204	    types: [created]
205	
206	permissions:
207	  contents: read
208	  pull-requests: read
209	
210	# Cancel an in-flight run when a new trigger fires for the same PR
211	# (or, for workflow_dispatch, the same ref). Avoids piling up Windows
212	# runners when a maintainer comments `/test-e2e` twice by accident or
213	# pushes a fixup commit during an active run.
214	concurrency:
215	  group: e2e-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.ref }}
216	  cancel-in-progress: true
217	
218	jobs:
219	  # Gate: only proceed if this is a workflow_dispatch OR a PR comment
220	  # whose first line is exactly "/test-e2e" (optionally followed by args)
221	  # from a trusted author. Without the author_association check, a fork
222	  # PR contributor could push malicious code, comment "/test-e2e", and
223	  # have it run with main's secrets — `issue_comment` events execute the
224	  # workflow defined on main but check out arbitrary refs.
225	  #
226	  # The body match is anchored to the start of the comment so an
227	  # unrelated comment mentioning `/test-e2e-something` or quoting the
228	  # trigger inside prose doesn't accidentally fire. GitHub Actions
229	  # `if:` expressions have no regex, so we approximate with two cases:
230	  # an exact-match body, or one that begins with the trigger followed
231	  # by a space (i.e. trigger plus arguments). This covers all practical
232	  # usage; an "issued the trigger followed only by a newline" edge case
233	  # is rare enough to re-comment.
234	  gate:
235	    if: >
236	      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
237	      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' &&
238	       github.event.issue.pull_request != null &&
239	       (github.event.comment.body == '/test-e2e' ||
240	        startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/test-e2e ')) &&
241	       (github.event.comment.author_association == 'OWNER' ||
242	        github.event.comment.author_association == 'MEMBER' ||
243	        github.event.comment.author_association == 'COLLABORATOR'))
244	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
245	    outputs:
246	      ref: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.ref }}
247	    steps:
248	      - id: resolve
249	        shell: bash

251	          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "issue_comment" ]]; then
252	            # Resolve PR head SHA so we test the PR's actual code.
253	            ref=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/pulls/${{ github.event.issue.number }}" --jq .head.sha)

255	            ref="${{ github.sha }}"
256	          fi

259	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

268	    steps:
269	      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
270	        with:
271	          ref: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.ref }}
272	
273	      - uses: jdx/mise-action@c37c93293d6b742fc901e1406b8f764f6fb19dac # v2.4.4
274	
275	      - name: Run e2e lifecycle tests
276	        # E2E_NO_AUTH=1 skips prompt-running tests (everything except
277	        # DetectAndEnable and HooksInstalledAfterEnable) on this first
278	        # workflow ship. The follow-up commit on this branch wires repo
279	        # secrets and removes this env var.
280	        env:
281	          E2E_NO_AUTH: "1"
282	        run: mise run test:e2e:lifecycle
283	```
284	
285	Notes:
286	
287	- `issue_comment` fires for both issues and PR comments; the `github.event.issue.pull_request != null` check filters to PR-only.
288	- The `author_association` gate restricts `/test-e2e` to OWNER / MEMBER / COLLABORATOR. This is **load-bearing security** — without it, anyone able to comment on a PR (including drive-by fork contributors) could exfiltrate repo secrets by triggering CI on their own pushed code. We accept the trade-off that external contributors must wait for a maintainer to comment `/test-e2e` on their behalf.
289	- `actions/checkout` with the resolved PR head SHA — without this, `issue_comment` checkouts default to `main`, which would test the wrong code.
290	- `fail-fast: false` so a Windows failure doesn't cancel Linux and vice-versa.
291	- The workflow does **not** add `permissions: pull-requests: write` or any write scopes; the gate token only needs to read PRs (`gh api repos/.../pulls/N`), which the default `github.token` can do.
292	- mise `tools` block: `tmux = "latest"` will fail to install on Windows. We scope it with mise's documented platform filter so the tmux install is skipped on `windows`:
293	  ```toml
294	  [tools]
295	  tmux = { version = "latest", os = ["linux", "macos"] }
296	  ```
297	  This is the standard mise syntax for OS-conditional tools and avoids relying on aliases like `'unix'` which are not part of mise's documented schema.
298	
299	### Permissions, secrets, auth
300	
301	The agents (Kiro, Pi) need API credentials to actually run. `e2e/agents/kiro.go` `Bootstrap()` and `e2e/agents/pi.go` `Bootstrap()` are both no-ops today. Six of the eight `TestLifecycle_*` tests call `RunPrompt` (or `StartSession` + `Send`), all of which spawn the agent binary against the real provider API. Without credentials, those six fail. Only `TestLifecycle_DetectAndEnable` and `TestLifecycle_HooksInstalledAfterEnable` would pass — they don't invoke the agent binary at all.
302	
303	This design **does not** wire CI secrets in this PR (separate concern, separate review surface), but it **does** add a deliberate skip-gate so that the very first CI run lands green rather than red:
304	
305	```go
306	// e2e/setup_test.go (or a per-agent precondition):
307	if os.Getenv("E2E_AGENT_AUTH_READY") != "1" {
308	    // Permit the workflow to land green while auth wiring is the
309	    // follow-up. Local runs without the env set still execute
310	    // everything (the gate only triggers when explicitly told CI is
311	    // unauthed) — so this does NOT silently degrade local dev.
312	    //
313	    // Inverted gate (opt-in to skip rather than opt-in to run) chosen
314	    // so a forgotten-secrets misconfig fails loudly instead of going
315	    // quiet.
316	}
317	```
318	
319	Concretely: tests that need agent auth call a `requireAgentAuth(t)` helper at the top, which `t.Skip`s when `E2E_AGENT_AUTH_READY` is unset *and* a sentinel like `E2E_NO_AUTH=1` (set only by the workflow on day 1) is set. Once secrets are wired in the follow-up, the workflow drops `E2E_NO_AUTH=1` and adds `E2E_AGENT_AUTH_READY=1`, all six tests un-skip, and we're done. Local runs default to "auth required" — the user always sees real failures.
320	
321	The helper lives in `e2e/setup_test.go` (same `package e2e` as `lifecycle_test.go`, so no import dance and no new file). Signature:
322	
323	```go
324	// requireAgentAuth skips the test when the workflow opts out of auth-gated tests
325	// via E2E_NO_AUTH=1. Local runs (env unset) always execute the test.
326	func requireAgentAuth(t *testing.T) {
327	    t.Helper()
328	    if os.Getenv("E2E_NO_AUTH") == "1" {
329	        t.Skip("skipping auth-gated test: E2E_NO_AUTH=1")
330	    }
331	}
332	```
333	
334	Follow-up commit on this branch (after the first green CI): set agent API keys as repo secrets, wire them into the workflow `env`, update `Bootstrap()` to write the appropriate config file, and remove `E2E_NO_AUTH` from the workflow.
335	
336	The exact secret names and config paths get discovered during that follow-up.
337	
338	## Risks and open questions
339	
340	| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
341	|---|---|---|
342	| ConPTY raw stream has TUI redraw artifacts that break prompt-pattern regex | Medium | Start simple. If flaky, swap to `charmbracelet/x/ansi` virtual screen. |
343	| Agents need API keys, no secrets set up | High | First CI run gated by `E2E_NO_AUTH=1` skip, follow-up commit wires secrets. |
344	| `cmd.Process.Kill()` on Windows leaks child processes | Low | Acceptable for short-lived agent calls; can upgrade to Job Objects later. |
345	| ConPTY `Send` 200ms-then-Enter timing is wrong for a non-tmux PTY (no tmux input buffering) | Low | If we see truncated input, drop the sleep — `\r` can be appended to the same write. |
346	| `conpty.Start` / `ConPty.Wait(ctx)` API drift between v0.1.4 and a later release | Low | API verified against v0.1.4 (`go doc`); pin in `go.mod`. |
347	
348	## Out of scope (explicitly)
349	
350	- macOS runner (`macos-latest`). Mac uses the existing tmux path; can be added to the matrix trivially later.
351	- Caching Go build cache via `actions/cache`.
352	- CI auth wiring for the agents.
353	- A virtual screen / full terminal emulator. Plain ANSI-strip first; upgrade only if needed.
354	- Refactoring `kiro.go` / `pi.go` `RunPrompt` to share logic. They're near-duplicates but that's a different cleanup.
355	
356	## File-by-file diff summary
357	
358	| File | Change |
359	|---|---|
360	| `e2e/go.mod` / `go.sum` | Add `github.com/UserExistsError/conpty` |
361	| `e2e/agents/tmux.go` | Add `//go:build !windows` |
362	| `e2e/agents/proc_unix.go` | **NEW** — `configureCmdProcAttr` (POSIX) |
363	| `e2e/agents/proc_windows.go` | **NEW** — `configureCmdProcAttr` (Windows) |
364	| `e2e/agents/conpty_windows.go` | **NEW** — `ConPTYSession`, `translateKey`, ANSI stripper |
365	| `e2e/agents/conpty_windows_test.go` | **NEW** — unit tests for `translateKey` |
366	| `e2e/agents/session_unix.go` | **NEW** — `newInteractiveSession` → tmux |
367	| `e2e/agents/session_windows.go` | **NEW** — `newInteractiveSession` → ConPTY |
368	| `e2e/agents/kiro.go` | Use `configureCmdProcAttr`; use `newInteractiveSession`; drop `s.stableAtSend = ""` |
369	| `e2e/agents/pi.go` | Use `configureCmdProcAttr`; use `newInteractiveSession`; drop `s.stableAtSend = ""` |
370	| `e2e/build.go` | Append `.exe` to `binPath` when `runtime.GOOS == "windows"` |
371	| `e2e/setup_test.go` | Skip tmux preflight on Windows; `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` → empty temp file; add `requireAgentAuth(t)` helper that `t.Skip`s when `E2E_NO_AUTH=1` |
372	| `e2e/lifecycle_test.go` | Call `requireAgentAuth(t)` at the top of each prompt-running test (all except `DetectAndEnable` and `HooksInstalledAfterEnable`) |
373	| `mise.toml` | Drop the entire `env GOCACHE=/tmp/...` prefix from `test:e2e:lifecycle` (just `go test ...`); scope `tmux` tool to `os = ["linux", "macos"]` |
374	| `mise-tasks/build` | Drop `GOCACHE=/tmp/...` (defensive only — script is bash-only) |
375	| `mise-tasks/test` | Drop `GOCACHE=/tmp/...` (defensive only — script is bash-only) |
376	| `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` | **NEW** — `workflow_dispatch` + author-gated `/test-e2e` PR comment trigger, OS matrix |
377	
378	## Order of work
379	
380	1. Cross-platform process attrs (`proc_unix.go`, `proc_windows.go`) — unblocks Windows compilation.
381	2. Build-tag tmux.go.
382	3. Add ConPTY dependency.
383	4. ConPTY session + tests for `translateKey`.
384	5. Session factory + wire up Pi/Kiro StartSession.
385	6. `setup_test.go` fixes (tmux preflight + `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` + `requireAgentAuth(t)` helper).
386	7. `lifecycle_test.go` add `requireAgentAuth(t)` calls at top of prompt-running tests.
387	8. `e2e/build.go` `.exe` suffix on Windows.
388	9. Drop GOCACHE overrides; scope mise `tmux` tool to unix.
389	10. Workflow file (with `E2E_NO_AUTH=1`).
390	11. Push branch, manually trigger workflow once via `workflow_dispatch` (author-gated path needs no PR comment), iterate on whatever breaks first.
391	12. Follow-up commit on this branch: wire agent API secrets, drop `E2E_NO_AUTH` from the workflow, update `Bootstrap()` to write the auth config.
392	
393	Step 1 is the hardest-to-reverse single decision (cross-platform refactor pattern) and it gates everything else, so it goes first. Steps 2–8 are mechanical once the pattern is set. # Windows E2E Tests — Design

## Goal

Run the existing `e2e/lifecycle_test.go` suite on Windows in CI so we can reproduce and verify Windows-specific bugs (like the one this branch is named for) without leaving the local machine.

The same suite already runs on Linux locally. We want:

1. A new on-demand workflow (`workflow_dispatch` + `/test-e2e` PR-comment trigger) so e2e doesn't run on every PR.
2. An OS matrix of `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest`.
3. The interactive `TestLifecycle_InteractiveSession` test to actually work on Windows (not skip), via ConPTY instead of tmux.

## Why this isn't a one-line workflow change

The e2e package today has three Linux-only assumptions baked in:

1. **`e2e/agents/tmux.go`** — drives Kiro/Pi interactive sessions via the `tmux` CLI. Windows has no tmux.
2. **`e2e/agents/kiro.go` and `pi.go`** — set `syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}` and call `syscall.Kill(-pid, ...)` on cancellation. Both are POSIX-only — `Setpgid` doesn't exist on `windows/syscall` and `syscall.Kill` doesn't either, so the package won't even **compile** on `GOOS=windows`.
3. **`e2e/setup_test.go`** — preflight checks for `tmux` in `PATH`, and sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`. Neither is correct on Windows.

So Windows support is: cross-platform refactor of the agent runner + a real ConPTY session impl + a couple of small test-setup fixes + the new workflow.

## ConPTY in one paragraph

**ConPTY** (Pseudo Console) is the native Windows pseudo-terminal API, available since Windows 10 1809. It's the OS-level thing that makes interactive TUIs work — the equivalent role tmux plays for us on Linux. PowerShell is *not* a substitute: it's a shell that runs *inside* a terminal, not a terminal provider, so child processes started under PowerShell with `Start-Process -RedirectStandardInput` see a pipe (not a TTY) and switch off interactive mode. We need a real PTY, and on Windows that means ConPTY. We'll use [`github.com/UserExistsError/conpty`](https://github.com/UserExistsError/conpty) (MIT, ~470⭐, actively used) as the Go wrapper.

ConPTY is lower-level than tmux: it gives us a process attached to a pseudo-console with raw read/write pipes. There's no built-in scrollback buffer and no named keys — we provide both ourselves.

## Component plan

### 1. Cross-platform process attributes

New build-tagged helpers in `e2e/agents/`:

- `proc_unix.go` (`//go:build !windows`):
  ```go
  func configureCmdProcAttr(cmd *exec.Cmd) {
      cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}
      cmd.Cancel = func() error { return syscall.Kill(-cmd.Process.Pid, syscall.SIGKILL) }
  }
  ```
- `proc_windows.go` (`//go:build windows`):
  ```go
  func configureCmdProcAttr(cmd *exec.Cmd) {
      cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{CreationFlags: 0x00000200} // CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP
      cmd.Cancel = func() error { return cmd.Process.Kill() }
  }
  ```

`kiro.go` and `pi.go` `RunPrompt` switch from inline syscall code to `configureCmdProcAttr(cmd)`.

Trade-off on Windows: we lose the `kill -pid` semantics that nuke the whole process group. `cmd.Process.Kill()` only kills the leader. For long-lived background TUIs this can leak children; for our short non-interactive `RunPrompt` invocations under context timeout, the child process is the agent itself and that's what we kill.

### 2. tmux.go gets `//go:build !windows`

Pure compile-out — tmux driver only exists on unix. Single-line change at the top of the file.

### 3. ConPTY session

New file `e2e/agents/conpty_windows.go` (`//go:build windows`).

```go
type ConPTYSession struct {
    cpty     *conpty.ConPty
    procDone <-chan struct{}
    exitErr  error

    bufMu sync.Mutex
    buf   []byte // ANSI-stripped rolling buffer, capped at 64 KiB

    cleanups     []func()
    stableAtSend string
}

func NewConPTYSession(name, dir string, unsetEnv []string, command string, args ...string) (*ConPTYSession, error)
```

Method-by-method:

- **`NewConPTYSession`**: builds command-line string (`command arg1 "arg with space" ...`), filters env removing `unsetEnv` entries, calls `conpty.Start(cmdLine, conpty.ConPtyWorkDir(dir), conpty.ConPtyEnv(env))`. Spawns one background goroutine reading from the conpty into the buffer (with mutex), and a second goroutine that calls `cpty.Wait(sessCtx)` and closes a `procDone` channel. (`Wait` takes a `context.Context` — confirmed against `github.com/UserExistsError/conpty v0.1.4` via `go doc`. The session stores its own `context.Background()`-derived `sessCtx` cancelled in `Close()` so `Wait` returns when the session is torn down.)
- **`Send(input)`**: mirrors `TmuxSession.Send` exactly — captures pre-state, calls `SendKeys(input)`, sleeps 200ms, calls `SendKeys("Enter")`, then runs the same 5-second "wait for content to change" loop using `stableContent`.
- **`SendKeys(keys ...string)`**: per key, look up `translateKey(k)` and write the resulting bytes to the conpty.
- **`WaitFor(pattern, timeout)`**: same loop and same `stableContent` settle logic as `TmuxSession.WaitFor`. Detects "process exited" by checking `procDone`.
- **`Capture()`**: returns the current ANSI-stripped buffer, trimmed of trailing newlines (matches tmux's `capture-pane -p` shape closely enough for the prompt-pattern regexes the tests use).
- **`Close()`**: runs cleanups, closes the conpty (terminates the process).

#### Key translator (shared by tmux SendKeys vocabulary)

```go
func translateKey(k string) string {
    switch k {
    case "Enter":              return "\r"
    case "Tab":                return "\t"
    case "Escape", "Esc":      return "\x1b"
    case "BSpace", "Backspace": return "\x7f"
    case "Up":                 return "\x1b[A"
    case "Down":               return "\x1b[B"
    case "Right":              return "\x1b[C"
    case "Left":               return "\x1b[D"
    case "Space":              return " "
    }
    if len(k) == 3 && (k[0] == 'C' || k[0] == 'c') && k[1] == '-' {
        c := k[2]
        if c >= 'a' && c <= 'z' { return string([]byte{c - 'a' + 1}) }
        if c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z' { return string([]byte{c - 'A' + 1}) }
    }
    return k // literal text
}
```

Vocabulary chosen to match the tmux key names already used by `TmuxSession.SendKeys`, so test code stays portable.

#### ANSI stripping

Tests look for prompt patterns like `>` (Kiro) and `\$\d` (Pi) — simple regex matches. We don't need a full terminal emulator. A regex strip of CSI sequences (`\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[a-zA-Z]`) plus OSC sequences (`\x1b\][^\x07]*\x07`) plus stripping `\r` (so CR-rewrites collapse) is sufficient.

Caveat: this CSI regex misses sequences with intermediate bytes (e.g. `\x1b[ q` cursor-style, `\x1b[1;2:3:4m` SGR with colon separators) and ST-terminated OSC (`\x1b\\` instead of `BEL`). If a TUI under test emits any of those and the leftover bytes confuse the prompt regexes, the upgrade path is `charmbracelet/x/ansi` which has a tested CSI parser plus a virtual screen. We start simple because the actual prompts (`>` and `\$\d`) are short enough to be unaffected by most stray escape bytes.

#### Buffer cap

Rolling 64 KiB. When append would overflow, drop the oldest 25 % so we never grow unbounded. Tests don't need long history — only the recent prompt area matters for regex matching.

### 4. Session factory

Tiny build-tagged constructor so `kiro.go` and `pi.go` don't need build tags themselves:

- `e2e/agents/session_unix.go` (`//go:build !windows`):
  ```go
  func newInteractiveSession(name, dir string, unsetEnv []string, cmd string, args ...string) (Session, error) {
      return NewTmuxSession(name, dir, unsetEnv, cmd, args...)
  }
  ```
- `e2e/agents/session_windows.go` (`//go:build windows`):
  ```go
  func newInteractiveSession(name, dir string, unsetEnv []string, cmd string, args ...string) (Session, error) {
      return NewConPTYSession(name, dir, unsetEnv, cmd, args...)
  }
  ```

`Pi.StartSession` / `Kiro.StartSession` switch from `NewTmuxSession(...)` to `newInteractiveSession(...)`. The redundant `s.stableAtSend = ""` lines (it's already the zero value after construction) get dropped — that removes the only direct field access through the concrete tmux type.

### 5. setup_test.go cross-platform fixes

Two small changes:

```go
// Old:
if _, err := exec.LookPath("tmux"); err != nil { /* warn */ }

// New:
if runtime.GOOS != "windows" {
    if _, err := exec.LookPath("tmux"); err != nil { /* warn */ }
}
```

```go
// Old:
os.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL", "/dev/null")

// New:
gc, _ := os.CreateTemp("", "e2e-gitconfig-*")
gc.Close()
os.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL", gc.Name())
// (cleanup on exit via t.Cleanup or defer in TestMain via os.Remove)
```

Empty temp file is functionally equivalent to `/dev/null` for git's purposes (an empty file = no global config) and works on every OS.

### 6. Drop `/tmp` GOCACHE overrides (and the `env` prefix)

The existing `mise-tasks/build`, `mise-tasks/test`, and `mise.toml` `test:e2e:lifecycle` task all use `env GOCACHE=/tmp/go-build-cache <command>`. `/tmp` doesn't exist on `windows-latest`, **and** the `env` utility itself is unix-only (cmd.exe / PowerShell don't have it on PATH). Options considered:

- **Keep but conditionalize via shell** — messy, three files.
- **Use `${TMPDIR}`** — inconsistent across OSes, doesn't fix the `env` issue.
- **Drop the entire `env GOCACHE=...` prefix** — Go's default cache (`%LocalAppData%\go-build` on Windows, `~/.cache/go-build` on Linux, `~/Library/Caches/go-build` on macOS) is correct for each OS. Chosen.

So `mise.toml`'s `test:e2e:lifecycle` `run = "env GOCACHE=/tmp/go-build-cache go test ..."` becomes `run = "go test ..."`. Removing only the `GOCACHE=...` and leaving `env go test ...` would still break Windows because `env` is not a Windows command — the whole prefix has to go.

CI caching can still happen via `actions/cache` keyed on `${{ runner.os }}` if we want it later — orthogonal to this change.

Note: `mise-tasks/build` and `mise-tasks/test` are bash scripts (`#!/usr/bin/env bash`). They do **not** run on Windows and the e2e workflow does not invoke them — it runs `mise run test:e2e:lifecycle` directly, which is defined inline in `mise.toml` as a portable `go test ...` command. The reason we still edit the bash scripts is purely to keep `/tmp` references from going stale; if they later get invoked from a Windows context (e.g. cross-compiling), they'd fail anyway for unrelated reasons. Not strictly required for this change — included as defensive cleanup.

### 6a. `BuildAgent` on Windows: `.exe` suffix

`e2e/build.go` `BuildAgent` produces `binPath := filepath.Join(outputDir, agentName)` and runs `go build -o binPath`. On Windows this would emit a literal extension-less file, which `exec.LookPath` and `cmd.exe`'s `PATHEXT` resolution will not find. Fix:

```go
binPath := filepath.Join(outputDir, agentName)
if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
    binPath += ".exe"
}
```

Add a corresponding `runtime` import (already imported in this file). This is a near-certainty (not a "verify on first run" item), so it lives in the file-by-file diff rather than the risk table.

### 7. Workflow file (`.github/workflows/e2e.yml`)

```yaml
name: E2E

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

# Cancel an in-flight run when a new trigger fires for the same PR
# (or, for workflow_dispatch, the same ref). Avoids piling up Windows
# runners when a maintainer comments `/test-e2e` twice by accident or
# pushes a fixup commit during an active run.
concurrency:
  group: e2e-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Gate: only proceed if this is a workflow_dispatch OR a PR comment
  # whose first line is exactly "/test-e2e" (optionally followed by args)
  # from a trusted author. Without the author_association check, a fork
  # PR contributor could push malicious code, comment "/test-e2e", and
  # have it run with main's secrets — `issue_comment` events execute the
  # workflow defined on main but check out arbitrary refs.
  #
  # The body match is anchored to the start of the comment so an
  # unrelated comment mentioning `/test-e2e-something` or quoting the
  # trigger inside prose doesn't accidentally fire. GitHub Actions
  # `if:` expressions have no regex, so we approximate with two cases:
  # an exact-match body, or one that begins with the trigger followed
  # by a space (i.e. trigger plus arguments). This covers all practical
  # usage; an "issued the trigger followed only by a newline" edge case
  # is rare enough to re-comment.
  gate:
    if: >
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' &&
       github.event.issue.pull_request != null &&
       (github.event.comment.body == '/test-e2e' ||
        startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/test-e2e ')) &&
       (github.event.comment.author_association == 'OWNER' ||
        github.event.comment.author_association == 'MEMBER' ||
        github.event.comment.author_association == 'COLLABORATOR'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      ref: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.ref }}
    steps:
      - id: resolve
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "issue_comment" ]]; then
            # Resolve PR head SHA so we test the PR's actual code.
            ref=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/pulls/${{ github.event.issue.number }}" --jq .head.sha)
          else
            ref="${{ github.sha }}"
          fi
          echo "ref=$ref" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  e2e:
    needs: gate
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.ref }}

      - uses: jdx/mise-action@c37c93293d6b742fc901e1406b8f764f6fb19dac # v2.4.4

      - name: Run e2e lifecycle tests
        # E2E_NO_AUTH=1 skips prompt-running tests (everything except
        # DetectAndEnable and HooksInstalledAfterEnable) on this first
        # workflow ship. The follow-up commit on this branch wires repo
        # secrets and removes this env var.
        env:
          E2E_NO_AUTH: "1"
        run: mise run test:e2e:lifecycle
```

Notes:

- `issue_comment` fires for both issues and PR comments; the `github.event.issue.pull_request != null` check filters to PR-only.
- The `author_association` gate restricts `/test-e2e` to OWNER / MEMBER / COLLABORATOR. This is **load-bearing security** — without it, anyone able to comment on a PR (including drive-by fork contributors) could exfiltrate repo secrets by triggering CI on their own pushed code. We accept the trade-off that external contributors must wait for a maintainer to comment `/test-e2e` on their behalf.
- `actions/checkout` with the resolved PR head SHA — without this, `issue_comment` checkouts default to `main`, which would test the wrong code.
- `fail-fast: false` so a Windows failure doesn't cancel Linux and vice-versa.
- The workflow does **not** add `permissions: pull-requests: write` or any write scopes; the gate token only needs to read PRs (`gh api repos/.../pulls/N`), which the default `github.token` can do.
- mise `tools` block: `tmux = "latest"` will fail to install on Windows. We scope it with mise's documented platform filter so the tmux install is skipped on `windows`:
  ```toml
  [tools]
  tmux = { version = "latest", os = ["linux", "macos"] }
  ```

### Permissions, secrets, auth

The agents (Kiro, Pi) need API credentials to actually run. `e2e/agents/kiro.go` `Bootstrap()` and `e2e/agents/pi.go` `Bootstrap()` are both no-ops today. Six of the eight `TestLifecycle_*` tests call `RunPrompt` (or `StartSession` + `Send`), all of which spawn the agent binary against the real provider API. Without credentials, those six fail. This design **does not** wire CI secrets in this PR (separate concern, separate review surface), but it **does** add a deliberate skip-gate so that the very first CI run lands green rather than red:

```go
// e2e/setup_test.go (or a per-agent precondition):

    // Permit the workflow to land green while auth wiring is the
    // follow-up. Local runs without the env set still execute
    // everything (the gate only triggers when explicitly told CI is
    // unauthed) — so this does NOT silently degrade local dev.
    //
    // Inverted gate (opt-in to skip rather than opt-in to run) chosen
    // so a forgotten-secrets misconfig fails loudly instead of going
    // quiet.
}
```

Concretely: tests that need agent auth call a `requireAgentAuth(t)` helper at the top, which `t.Skip`s when `E2E_AGENT_AUTH_READY` is unset *and* a sentinel like `E2E_NO_AUTH=1` (set only by the workflow on day 1) is set. Once secrets are wired in the follow-up, the workflow drops `E2E_NO_AUTH=1` and adds `E2E_AGENT_AUTH_READY=1`, all six tests un-skip, and we're done. Local runs default to "auth required" — the user always sees real failures.

The helper lives in `e2e/setup_test.go` (same `package e2e` as `lifecycle_test.go`, so no import dance and no new file). Signature:

```go

// via E2E_NO_AUTH=1. Local runs (env unset) always execute the test.
func requireAgentAuth(t *testing.T) {
    t.Helper()
    if os.Getenv("E2E_NO_AUTH") == "1" {
        t.Skip("skipping auth-gated test: E2E_NO_AUTH=1")
    }
}
```
